title: kate-ui: list the command palette entries
summary: command_entries returns the named commands the window offers, each with its key binding, and command_rows ranks them for a query. Every binding in the list round-trips through keys::command_for_binding, which the test checks.

lane.reason: A Cursor local agent on the owner Mac codes this packet. The file has no GPUI import, but kate-ui tests run in the rust (macos-15) job and the Mac lane owns crates/kate-ui.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: The bindings are cmd-s, cmd-z, shift-cmd-z, cmd-a, ctrl-space, ctrl-], ctrl-[, f5, cmd-d, cmd-alt-[, alt-shift-down, alt-shift-up. command_rows uses kate_core::fuzzy_rank over the names; detail is the binding or an empty string; positions index the label. The test every_entry_binding_round_trips asserts for each entry with a binding that keys::command_for_binding(binding) equals Some(entry.command), and that command_rows("undo", 5) has Undo first. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: palette::tests::every_entry_binding_round_trips
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because command_entries does not exist. After the change every binding maps back to its command and the query undo ranks Undo first.
